findings.explanation: The module encrypts its notification topic with a customer-managed key (kms_key_name = var.key), and the example supplies google_kms_crypto_key.cloudsource.id. Nothing anywhere grants the Pub/Sub P4SA (service-<project>@gcp-sa-pubsub.iam.gserviceaccount.com) roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on that key, so topic creation is rejected by the API and terraform apply fails on a clean project. At the module root holden can only return UNKNOWN for HLD_GCP_458 and HLD_GCP_463 because var.key is an unbound module input; scanning example/examplea resolves it and HLD_GCP_458 fails there outright. Reported here because .holden.yaml scans '.' with targets [gha], so the module-root gate never sees the resolved verdict.
findings.remediation: Add the service identity and the key grant to example/examplea, and make the topic depend on the grant so ordering is deterministic (this is what HLD_GCP_463 is checking). google_project_service_identity requires the google-beta provider, which the example's required_providers must also declare.
findings.title: CMEK-encrypted Pub/Sub topic has no key grant for the Pub/Sub service agent, so the example cannot apply
findings.verification: HLD_GCP_458 no longer fails and HLD_GCP_463 resolved from UNKNOWN to pass at example/examplea; tofu validate clean.

findings.explanation: var.repository_readers carries an explicit validation rejecting allUsers and allAuthenticatedUsers. var.iam_bindings grants IAM on the same repository through google_sourcerepo_repository_iam_member.binding and carries no such guard, so a consumer can pass { "roles/source.reader" = ["allUsers"] } and publish the entire source repository, including anything ever committed to its history, to the internet. This is the inconsistency pattern: the author clearly intends the guard, and applied it to the newer variable but not the older one. holden's HLD_GCP_312 targets exactly this and returns UNKNOWN at both roots because member resolves through a for_each over an unbound map, so the engine cannot decide it either way.
findings.remediation: Mirror the guard that var.repository_readers already has onto every member list in var.iam_bindings, so the module refuses public grants at plan time regardless of which variable the consumer uses.
findings.title: var.iam_bindings has no allUsers/allAuthenticatedUsers guard, while var.repository_readers on the same repository does
findings.verification: Verified empirically: passing {"roles/source.reader" = ["allUsers"]} now fails tofu validate with the new error message. HLD_GCP_312 still reports UNKNOWN by design — holden evaluates resource attributes, not variable validation blocks, so the engine cannot observe this guard.

findings.explanation: Google announced on 2024-06-17 that Cloud Source Repositories is no longer available to projects that had not previously used it. The service still runs for existing users but is not receiving feature work, and a deprecated service is one that stops receiving security hardening while remaining in the blast radius. No deterministic rule covers service-lifecycle status, since it is external product information rather than a config attribute. This is a roadmap concern rather than an exploitable weakness — flagged so it is a deliberate decision rather than an unnoticed one.
findings.remediation: No code change. Confirm the consuming projects are grandfathered in, and record whether this module is intentionally maintenance-only. If new consumers are expected, plan a migration to Secure Source Manager or an external Git host.
findings.title: Module is built on Cloud Source Repositories, which Google closed to new customers in June 2024

suggested_suppressions.outcome: User marked var.key sensitive = true instead of suppressing HLD_TF_050. That propagated the sensitivity to output.topic and output.dead_letter_topic, which holden then flagged as HLD_TF_080; both outputs were marked sensitive = true in response. Both policies now pass.
suggested_suppressions.reason:
var.key is matched on its name alone, but it holds a Cloud KMS crypto key resource ID, not key material. It is assigned only to google_pubsub_topic.kms_key_name, and the example supplies google_kms_crypto_key.cloudsource.id — a non-sensitive computed attribute. A key ID of the form projects/

/locations//keyRings//cryptoKeys/ is a public identifier that appears in IAM policy documents and the GCP console; it grants nothing on its own. This is the reference-to-a-secret vs literal-secret distinction. Marking it sensitive = true would also redact kms_key_name from plan output, making CMEK misconfiguration harder to review at the point where review matters.
suggested_suppressions.suppression_comment: # holden:ignore:HLD_TF_050: var.key is a KMS crypto key resource ID (a public identifier), not key material — nothing secret to redact
